changes.text: The increase in net cash used in operating activities during the six months ended September 30, 2026, compared to the prior period, was due to $88,583 of unfavorable changes in operating assets and liabilities partially offset by $35,088 of favorable net income after non-cash adjustments that included the impact from IEEPA tariff net refunds and related interest income. Changes in operating assets and liabilities were primarily due to unfavorable impacts from (1) net trade accounts receivable from timing of sales and respective receipts; (2) timing of net receipts and sales of inventory; and (3) timing of tax payments and receipts, partially offset by favorable impacts from (4) net trade accounts payable from timing of receipts of goods and services and related disbursements, including accommodations provided under cost-sharing arrangements with independent manufacturers for IEEPA tariff refunds; and (5) timing of derivative contract cash settlements recorded to prepaid expenses and other current assets.
changes.prior_text: The increase in net cash provided by operating activities during the six months ended September 30, 2025, compared to the prior period, was due to $51,227 of favorable net income after non-cash adjustments partially offset by $29,094 of unfavorable changes in operating assets and liabilities. Changes in operating assets and liabilities were primarily due to unfavorable impacts from (1) timing of derivative contract cash settlements, (2) higher cost and earlier purchases of inventory to support elevated demand for our products and the transition to our European 3PL, partially offset by favorable impacts from (3) net trade accounts receivable from timing of sales and respective receipts, (4) net trade accounts payable from timing of receipts of goods and services and related disbursements, and (5) timing of tax payments and receipts.

changes.text: We previously paid an aggregate of approximately $119,000 in gross IEEPA tariffs. During the three and six months ended September 30, 2026, we recorded approximately $46,000 of IEEPA tariff net refunds as a reduction to cost of sales and approximately $3,000 of related interest as interest income within our condensed consolidated statements of comprehensive income. The net effect of the refunds reflects accommodations provided under cost-sharing arrangements with our independent manufacturers and other relevant factors. Subsequent to September 30, 2026, through October 8, 2026, we received additional IEEPA tariff net refunds that will be recognized in our condensed consolidated financial statements in the third fiscal quarter which, combined with the refunds previously received, total approximately $87,900, plus associated interest for a total of approximately $4,700. Refer to Note 7, “Commitments and Contingencies,” of our condensed consolidated financial statements in Part I, Item 1 within this Quarterly Report for further information on tariff refunds, including related accounting treatment.

Gross Profit. Gross margin increased to 58.8% from 56.0% compared to the prior period, primarily due to benefits from IEEPA tariff net refunds after accommodations provided under cost-sharing arrangements with our independent manufacturers, as well as favorable brand product mix, and favorable full-price selling.
changes.prior_text: Gross Profit. Gross margin decreased to 56.0% from 56.3% compared to the prior period, primarily due to unfavorable channel mix as wholesale revenue growth outpaced DTC revenue growth, higher promotional activity for the HOKA brand, as well as incremental tariffs on US goods impacting the current fiscal quarter, partially offset by favorable product mix shifts, benefits from price increases, and favorable foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations. The net impact of tariff-related variables was not material in the current period due to the timing of the implementation of our mitigation strategies, including price increases and earlier inventory shipments in advance of the incremental tariffs.

changes.text: Tariffs and Related Refunds. Evolving trade policies, including tariffs and other import restrictions, continue to expose us to risks associated with our sourcing and manufacturing concentrations. The scope and duration of current and proposed tariff regimes, as well as the amount and timing of future refunds of previously paid IEEPA tariffs remain uncertain. We continue to pursue mitigation strategies but do not expect these efforts to fully offset incremental tariff costs we expect to incur during the current fiscal year, excluding any future IEEPA tariff refunds.

changes.text: The preparation of our condensed consolidated financial statements in accordance with US GAAP requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the amounts reported. Management bases these estimates and assumptions upon historical experience, existing and known circumstances, authoritative accounting pronouncements, and other factors it believes to be reasonable. In addition, management has considered the potential impact of macroeconomic and geopolitical factors on our financial condition, results of operations, and liquidity, including inflationary pressures, increased tariffs, tariff refunds received and the recoverability of remaining tariff refund claims, rising supply chain costs, high interest rates, foreign currency exchange rate volatility, escalating global conflicts, changes in discretionary spending, and recession risks. Although the full impact of these factors, including the amount, timing, and realization of certain tariff refunds, is unknown, management believes it has made appropriate accounting estimates and assumptions based on the facts and circumstances available as of the reporting date. However, actual results could differ materially from these estimates and assumptions, which may result in material effects on our financial condition, results of operations, and liquidity. Refer to Note 1, “General,” of our condensed consolidated financial statements in Part I, Item 1 within this Quarterly Report, for further discussion of our significant accounting policies and use of estimates.
